scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs support for cities while doubting the reason that culture lives mainly in them; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Great cities can be the proud showcases of an entire nation.
One claim holds that governments must ensure their major cities receive the funding they need to thrive, on the reason that culture is preserved and generated primarily in cities.
I agree that cities deserve support, but I doubt the reason and believe the rest of the nation needs funding too.
First, major cities genuinely do need and deserve strong government support.
Cities hold much of a nation's business, services, and people in one busy place.
For example, a well-funded city can offer good transport, hospitals, and jobs to millions.
This shows that supporting cities can benefit a large share of a nation's people.
Thriving cities can also drive the whole country's economy forward.
Neglected cities, by contrast, can fall into poverty, crime, and decay.
To this extent, funding major cities is clearly wise.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the reason is doubtful

sentences.text: Second, however, the reason that culture lives primarily in cities is doubtful.
Much of a nation's tradition is created and preserved in its villages and countryside.
Consider the folk songs, crafts, and customs that survive best far from any major city.
Such traditions show that culture does not belong to cities alone.
Rural areas also need funding for schools, roads, and hospitals just as much as cities do.
Pouring money only into cities could leave the rest of the nation neglected and poor.
Government support, then, should reach the whole nation, not mainly its cities.
In conclusion, major cities do deserve the funding they need to thrive.
But the reason that culture lives only in cities is mistaken, and rural areas need support too.
The wisest governments fund their cities while never neglecting the regions beyond them.
